recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further core source work is indicated for FHIR-14192 unless the Security WG later makes a new final decision to redesign the remaining BTG guidance, especially the experimental HTTP Category mechanism.
issue_request: FHIR-14192 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-I issue asking to clarify the Break the Glass description, especially the risks of treating an HTTP header as a security mechanism, the need for authorization, consent, access-control, PurposeOfUse vocabulary, AuditEvent linkage, top-level Security-page visibility, and client/user signaling.
initial_application: The issue was applied in git-svn commit e0fb4dcd4e8de6a68f5c9e68dfd37b64ab9b1007, whose message explicitly says GF#14192 and svn revision 14473. That patch updated source/security-labels.html with BTG purpose-of-use request representation and dragon-note responsibilities for initiation, authorization, consent/access control, and AuditEvent representation.
additional_context: Later final BTG issues changed how the original 2018 text should be read now: FHIR-5935 preserved the no-policy/no-protocol caveat, FHIR-9167 added the AuditEvent example and references, FHIR-27917 established BTG for the OperationOutcome hint, FHIR-42756 corrected the BTG terminology URL, FHIR-42757 added the OAuth purpose-of-use alternative, FHIR-53885 moved the standalone section from Security Labels to Security, and FHIR-19499 resolved that prior CPs already made related clarifications.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current Security page already defines Break the Glass, links v3-ActReason#BTG, explains that FHIR does not define policy or protocol around such requests, lists when/how/authorization/consent/audit/client-hint responsibilities, and gives OAuth and HTTP Category examples. Restoring or duplicating the old Security Labels section would contradict the later FHIR-53885 move.
